en: Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to care for premature babies in rural Philippine areas.
The Philippine eagle, also known as the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird of the Philippines.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines is the highest tribunal and leads the judicial branch of government.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the Cordillera mountains over two thousand years ago.
The Ati-Atihan festival in Kalibo, Aklan, honors the Santo Niño with dancers wearing indigenous tribal costumes.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system that uses specific characters to represent Tagalog syllables.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river flowing directly into the sea.
Filipino citizens must be at least eighteen years old to register and vote in national elections.
National Scientist Dr. Ramon Barba invented a potassium nitrate technology that makes mango trees flower year-round.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white flower, was officially declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
Chief Lapulapu led native warriors who defeated Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan in the 1521 Battle of Mactan.
